answer.reasoning: I treated the opening, recap, and motivation for computer graphics as the first content step, then cut at the bridge into the pipeline review. Stage 2 is split into the idea of modeling transformation, matrix representation of transformations, and the composite-transformation worked example. Stage 3 is split into why color/lighting matters, the physical basis of color perception, the simple lighting model, attenuation, extensions for colored/multiple lights, and intensity mapping. I merged the colored-light and multiple-light-source discussion because the multiple-source formula depends on the colored-light definitions, and I made the closing summary a final standalone segment.

segments.subgoal: Explain why computer graphics is relevant to understanding rendering and resource optimization in virtual reality.
Describe the five stages of the 3D graphics pipeline and identify which stages this lecture covers.
Explain the purpose of modeling or geometric transformation and identify the basic transformations used to assemble objects into a scene.
Describe how 2D and 3D transformations are represented by homogeneous-coordinate matrices and how a point is transformed by matrix multiplication.
Explain how to form composite transformation matrices and use them to compute transformed world-coordinate vertices in a worked example.
Explain why color computation is needed in the pipeline and distinguish lighting models from shading models.
Describe how light from a source is incident on a surface, reflected, and perceived as color.
Describe the simple lighting model that computes reflected light intensity as ambient, diffuse, and specular components using vector dot products.
Explain how radial and angular attenuation factors modify light-source intensity in a lighting model.
Describe how colored light sources and multiple light sources extend the lighting model.
Explain how continuous lighting-model intensities are mapped to finite device-supported intensity values and bit patterns.
Summarize the main points of the lecture.
